title: Bài 6: Các Dụ Ngôn Về Nước Thiên Đàng
subtitle: Parables of the Kingdom — Matthew 13 (sower, mustard seed, treasure, pearl); Matthew 25 (ten virgins, talents) · Ngữ pháp: Reported speech: statements (say/tell + that-clause, tense backshift), questions (ask + if/whether/wh-word), commands (tell/ask + to-infinitive)
scripture: Matthew 13 (sower, mustard seed, treasure, pearl); Matthew 25 (ten virgins, talents)
grammar_topic: Reported speech: statements (say/tell + that-clause, tense backshift), questions (ask + if/whether/wh-word), commands (tell/ask + to-infinitive)
pronunciation: Connected speech — elision: the /t/ and /d/ that disappear between consonants (next day, first time, must be, kind of)
pronunciation_detail: In natural, connected English, sounds often disappear. When /t/ or /d/ sits between two consonants, native speakers usually drop it — the word is still understood from the context. Vietnamese learners often pronounce every sound carefully ("next day" with a clear /t/), which sounds slow and foreign. Learn to drop the sound: next day — the /t/ disappears: "neks day" /neks deɪ/. first time — the /t/ disappears: "firs time" /fɜːs taɪm/. must be — the /t/ disappears: "mus be" /mʌs biː/. kind of — the /d/ disappears: "kine of" /kaɪn əv/. last night — the /t/ disappears: "las night" /lɑːs naɪt/. old friend — the /d/ disappears: "ol friend" /əʊl frend/. Rule: the sound disappears only between consonants, and only in fast, natural speech. In slow, careful speech — reading the Bible aloud in church, for example — you may keep the sound. Never drop a sound at the start of a word, and never drop /t/ or /d/ before a vowel: say "next hour" with the /t/ (next + vowel), but "next day" without it (next + consonant). Practice: listen to the lesson audio and shadow it — copy the elision exactly. Then read these sentences aloud twice: once slow and careful (all sounds), once natural (with elision): "The first time I heard the parable, I must be honest — it was kind of hard to understand."

grammar.title: Reported speech: statements (say/tell + that-clause, tense backshift), questions (ask + if/whether/wh-word), commands (tell/ask + to-infinitive)
grammar.explain:
When we tell someone what another person said, we usually shift the tense back one step — because the words were spoken in the past. This is called reported speech (or indirect speech).

Structure 1: Reported Statements — say / tell + that Direct: Jesus said, “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed.” Reported: Jesus said that the kingdom of heaven was like a mustard seed. (In Bible retelling, the present tense is often kept when the truth is still true: “Jesus said that the kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed” is also correct.) Use say with no person, and tell with a person: “He said that he would return.” — “He told his servants that he would return.” Never say “He said me that…” Backshift table — direct speech to reported speech: Present simple to past simple: “The seed is the word of God.” to “The teacher said that the seed was the word of God.”

Present continuous to past continuous: “The thorns are growing.” to “He said that the thorns were growing.” Will to would: “I will return.” to “The master said that he would return.” Can to could: “I can explain it.” to “Hoa said that she could explain it.” Present perfect to past perfect: “I have found the treasure.” to “He said that he had found the treasure.”

Structure 2: Reported Questions — ask + if / whether / Wh-word Yes/No questions use if or whether, and the word order becomes statement order (no do / does / did, no question mark): Direct: “Is the kingdom like a pearl?” Reported: “Lan asked if the kingdom was like a pearl.” Wh-questions keep the question word: Direct: “What does the parable mean?” Reported: “The disciple asked what the parable meant.”

Structure 3: Reported Commands — tell / ask + person + to + verb Direct: “Watch and be ready.” Reported: “Jesus told the disciples to watch and be ready.” Direct: “Use my money well.” Reported: “The master told his servants to use his money well.” For a negative command, use not to: “Do not be afraid” to “He told them not to be afraid.”

Watch out: do not keep the question word order in reported questions — say “He asked what the parable meant”, not “He asked what did the parable mean”. And remember: say takes no person (“He said that…”), tell always takes a person (“He told me that…”).

reading_passage: Jesus loved to teach with parables — short, simple stories that carry a deep truth about the kingdom of heaven. He told His disciples that the kingdom is like a sower who went out to sow his seed. Some seed fell along the path, and the birds ate it. Some fell on rocky ground, where it grew quickly but had no root, so the sun burned it. Some fell among thorns, and the thorns choked it. But some seed fell on good soil, and it gave a rich harvest — a hundred, sixty, or thirty times as much as was sown. The seed is the word of God, and the soil is the heart that hears it. Then Jesus said that the kingdom is like a grain of mustard seed. It is the smallest of all seeds, yet when it grows, it becomes the largest of all garden plants, and the birds come and rest in its branches. The kingdom starts small, but it grows very great. He also said that the kingdom is like treasure hidden in a field. When a man found it, he sold all that he had and bought that field. It is also like a merchant who found one pearl of great value, and sold everything to buy it. The kingdom is worth everything we have. In Matthew 25, Jesus told two more parables about being ready. Ten virgins waited for the bridegroom, but only five were wise and took oil for their lamps. And a master gave his servants talents and asked them to use his money well. The faithful servants were rewarded, and the master said, 'Well done, good and faithful servant.' The parables ask us a question: what kind of soil are we, and are we ready for the King?

reading_comprehension.q: 1. Why did Jesus teach in parables?
reading_comprehension.a: He teaches with short stories (parables) that show what the kingdom of heaven is like, so that ordinary people can understand deep truths.

reading_comprehension.q: 2. What does the mustard seed teach us about the kingdom of heaven?
reading_comprehension.a: It grows from the smallest seed into the largest garden plant — the kingdom starts small but grows very great.

reading_comprehension.q: 3. What did the man who found the treasure and the merchant who found the pearl have in common?
reading_comprehension.a: Both the man and the merchant sold everything they had, because the kingdom is worth more than anything else.

reading_comprehension.q: 4. What is the difference between the wise and the foolish virgins?
reading_comprehension.a: Five were wise and took oil for their lamps; five were foolish and took no oil, so they were not ready when the bridegroom came.

reading_comprehension.q: 5. What did the master do when he returned in the parable of the talents?
reading_comprehension.a: He rewarded the faithful servants, who had used his gifts well, and said, 'Well done, good and faithful servant.'

listening_questions.q: 1. How did Jesus often teach the people?
listening_questions.a: With parables — short stories that show what the kingdom of heaven is like.

listening_questions.q: 2. In the parable of the sower, which seed gave a harvest?
listening_questions.a: Some seed fell on good soil and gave a harvest — a hundred, sixty, or thirty times as much.

listening_questions.q: 3. What did Jesus say the seed and the soil mean?
listening_questions.a: The seed is the word of God, and the soil is the heart of the person who hears it.

listening_questions.q: 4. What did Jesus say the kingdom of heaven is like?
listening_questions.a: Like a grain of mustard seed — the smallest seed, but it grows into the largest garden plant.

listening_questions.q: 5. What two things did Jesus say the kingdom is like, and what did the men do?
listening_questions.a: Like treasure hidden in a field, and like a merchant who found one pearl of great value — both sold everything to have it.

listening_questions.q: 6. What did the master in the parable of the talents say and ask?
listening_questions.a: He said that he would return, and he asked his servants to use his money well. The faithful servants doubled what they had been given.

exercises.title: Exercise 1: Elision — The Disappearing /t/ and /d/
exercises.instruction: In fast, natural speech, /t/ and /d/ often disappear between two consonants. Write how each phrase really sounds, and say which sound is dropped.

exercises.title: Exercise 2: Reported Statements — Say and Tell
exercises.instruction: Change each sentence into reported speech. Use 'said that...' and shift the tense back one step (present simple to past simple, will to would, can to could).

exercises.title: Exercise 3: Reported Questions and Commands
exercises.instruction: Change each question or command into reported speech. For questions use 'asked' + if/whether or the question word (no question mark, no do/does). For commands use 'told/asked + person + to + verb'.

exercises.title: Exercise 4: Vocabulary Matching
exercises.instruction: Match each word with its correct definition.

exercises.title: Exercise 5: Reading — True or False?
exercises.instruction: Read the passage in Section 5 again. Mark T (true) or F (false). Correct the false sentences.

exercises.title: Exercise 6: Translation Lab (Vietnamese to English)
exercises.instruction: Translate into natural English. Use reported speech (said that / asked if / told ... to ...).

speaking_task: Roleplay in pairs (3 minutes): Student A tells Student B about one parable from Matthew 13 or 25, using reported speech ('Jesus said that...', 'The master told his servants to...', 'The disciple asked...'). Student B asks two questions ('What did Jesus say about...?'). Use at least 4 reported-speech sentences and 5 vocabulary words from Section 3. Practise elision: say 'next day', 'first time', 'must be', 'kind of' the natural way, with the /t/ or /d/ dropped.
writing_task: Write a short retelling (80-100 words) of one parable from Matthew 13 or 25, in reported speech. Begin: 'Jesus told his disciples a parable. He said that...' Use at least 4 reported-speech sentences (said that / told ... to ... / asked ...) and 5 vocabulary words from Section 3.

written: A. Change these 5 direct sentences into reported speech: 1) Jesus: 'The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed.' 2) The master: 'I will come back soon.' 3) Hoa: 'I can explain the parable of the talents.' 4) The teacher: 'Watch and be ready.' 5) Lan: 'Are you ready for the bridegroom?'
B. Write 6 sentences retelling the parable of the talents in reported speech (use: said that, told, asked, would, could). Begin: 'The master called his servants and said that...'
